name: Olympic swimming pool
headline: length
subtitle: Pool standard for the Olympic Games and World Aquatics Championships
description: An Olympic swimming pool is 50 metres long between the electronic touch panels at each end, and World Aquatics allows only 1 cm of extra length and none short. Pools used at the Olympic Games must be at least 25 m wide, enough for eight 2.5 m lanes plus a 2.5 m buffer space on each side. World Aquatics' current certification rules call for a water depth of at least 2.5 m, rising to 3 m when the pool is shared with artistic swimming.

measures.label: Length
measures.note: Between the touch panels of the automatic officiating equipment; tolerance +0.010 m / -0.000 m

measures.label: Width
measures.note: Minimum for permanent pools at the Olympic Games; temporary pools are 26 m

measures.label: Minimum depth
measures.note: Olympic Games and World Aquatics Championships 50 m pools (certification rules in force from 1 January 2024); 3 m when also used for artistic swimming

measures.label: Lane width
measures.note: Olympic Games lane width; 8 lanes with a 2.5 m space outside lanes 1 and 8

facts.text: Without touch panels, the wall-to-wall distance of a 50 m pool must be between 50.020 m and 50.030 m so that the panels can be fitted and still leave 50.000 m.
Olympic Games pools have 8 lanes, while World Championships pools have 10.
The earlier 2021-2025 Facilities Rules set the Olympic pool minimum depth at 2 m, with 3 m recommended for multi-discipline use.

sources.title: Swimming Pool Certification (in force as from 1 January 2024)
FINA Facilities Rules 2021-2025, FR 2.2 Swimming Facilities for Olympic Games and World Championships

caveats: Width and depth are minimums for Olympic Games pools; real pools can be wider or deeper.
No official source found gives a water volume, so none is listed.
